iSupport-D Privacy Notice and Consent Statement
iSupport-D Privacy Notice and Consent Statement

iSupport-D is a digital education and support platform developed and operated by the iSupport-D research team (“we”, “us”, “our”) through Swinburne University of Technology and National Ageing Research Institute.
We are committed to protecting personal information and complying with:
The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and Australian Privacy Principles (APPs)
Relevant State and Territory privacy laws
The National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research
Where applicable, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and other international data protection laws.
This Notice explains how we collect, use, disclose, store and otherwise handle personal information when you access or use the iSupport-D website or mobile application (“Platform”).

By registering for or using the Platform, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Privacy Notice and consent to the handling of your personal information as described.
Where required by law, separate research consent will be obtained before collecting sensitive or health-related information.

We may collect information reasonably necessary to operate the Platform, including name, email address, phone number (optional), country, region, or general location, user role (e.g., family carer, health professional, researcher), purpose of using the platform, and login credentials and authentication data.

If you participate in research components, we may collect:
Responses to questionnaires, surveys, or program activities
Feedback on usability and acceptability
Wellbeing, caregiving, or dementia-related experiences
Other health or sensitive information relevant to approved research aims
Sensitive information will only be collected with explicit informed consent and in accordance with ethics approval.

When using the Platform, technical data may be collected automatically, including:
IP address
Device identifiers
Browser type and operating system
Usage patterns and session duration
Navigation paths and feature engagement
This data supports system security, analytics, service optimisation and research evaluation.
Data Breach Response & Notification Clause (Platform + Governance Document)

The Platform may use cookies or similar technologies to:
Maintain login sessions
Remember user preferences
Analyse traffic and usage trends
Improve functionality and performance
Users may adjust browser settings to refuse cookies; however, some Platform functions may be affected.

We collect, use and disclose personal information for purposes including:
Account creation and authentication
Delivery and personalisation of program content
Monitoring engagement and improving user experience
Conducting research and evaluation
Reporting to ethics committees and funding bodies
Complying with legal and regulatory obligations
Protecting system integrity and preventing misuse
We do not sell personal information and do not use personal information for commercial marketing.

The Platform may use data analytics, machine learning, or AI-enabled tools to:
Tailor content and support pathways
Identify general usage patterns
Improve program design and delivery
These tools are designed to support education and research. They do not make clinical diagnoses, treatment decisions, or legally significant decisions about users.
Users should not rely solely on Platform outputs when making health or caregiving decisions.

iSupport-D is conducted under approval from a registered Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC).
Participation in research is voluntary. You may:
Decline participation
Skip research questions
Withdraw consent at any time
Withdrawal will not affect access to general educational content unless required by the research protocol.
Ethics Approval Reference: [Insert HREC details].

Personal information may be disclosed to:
Authorised members of the research team
Collaborating universities or research institutions
IT hosting providers and software developers
Data analysis service providers
Government agencies or regulators where required or authorised by law
All third parties are required to comply with confidentiality and data protection obligations.

Some service providers or research collaborators may be located outside Australia.
By using the Platform, you acknowledge that your personal information may be transferred to and stored in other countries.
We take reasonable steps to ensure overseas recipients handle information consistently with Australian privacy standards or applicable international laws.

We implement reasonable safeguards including:
Encryption and secure hosting
Restricted access controls
Audit and monitoring processes
Staff confidentiality obligations
Personal information will be retained only as long as necessary for research, legal and reporting requirements and then securely destroyed or permanently de-identified where practicable.

Australian Users
You may request access to or correction of personal information we hold about you.
International Users (including EU/EEA)
Where applicable, you may have rights to:
Access personal data
Request rectification
Request erasure
Restrict processing
Object to certain processing
Request data portability
Lodge a complaint with a data protection authority
Requests may be made using the contact details below.

If you believe your privacy has been breached, you may contact us.
We will investigate and respond within a reasonable timeframe.
If you are not satisfied, you may contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) or relevant overseas authority.

The Platform may contain links to third-party websites.
We are not responsible for their privacy practices. Users should review their policies before providing information.

The Platform provides general educational information and self-support tools.
It is not intended to replace professional medical, psychological, legal, or aged-care advice.
Users should seek advice from appropriately qualified professionals regarding individual circumstances.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, the iSupport-D research team and affiliated institutions exclude liability for any loss, damage, or harm arising from reliance on Platform content, technical interruptions, data transmission risks, or unauthorised access beyond our reasonable control.
Nothing in this Notice excludes rights that cannot be excluded under applicable consumer or privacy laws.

This project is supported by the Australian Government through the Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF).
The views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect Government policy.
School of Health Sciences, Swinburne University of Technology, John Street, Hawthorn, VIC 3122, Australia
This Privacy Notice should be read together with the Platform Terms of Use and Research Participant Information and Consent Form (PICF).
